summary:
Every rating's SP category is riding a perfect 3-for-3 over the last two weeks, with R1, R2, R3 and R4 all posting 100% (n=3) on starting-pitcher plays and a live 3W streak across the board. That's thin sample size, but it lines up with the season-long signal: trends+sp is the best-agreeing category combo at 58% (370-268, n=638), so when SP and trends point the same direction today, lean in. The flip side is just as loud — bullpen_fatigue is ice cold everywhere, 0-3 across all four ratings with a 5-game losing streak on every single rating. If today's board has a bullpen_fatigue lean fighting against an SP or trends pick, fade the fatigue angle without hesitation.

On today's slate, R2 is the rating to trust first. It's the only one showing positive unit movement in the 14-day strong-play window (+1.0u on a 2-1 mark) and it's hot over 30 days at 70% (7-3, +3.0u, n=10) — both comfortably ahead of R1, R3 and R4, which are all flat at +0.0u in the same windows. If R2 and another rating both tag a game as a strong play, that's your highest-confidence spot today. Team-wise, keep eyes on LAD and BOS if either is on the board — LAD strong plays are hitting 80% (28-7, +27.0u) and BOS strong plays sit at 76% (22-7, +19.0u), the two best marks in the team table. Conversely, if NYY shows up as a model pick, treat it skeptically: 49% overall (23-24) and a money-losing -4.0u on strong plays, the only team leader in the red. With all four ratings showing identical 3-game sample windows today, the categories matter more than which rating number you're reading — trends+sp agreement remains the sharpest filter on the board, and anything stacking that combo with an R2 strong-play tag is the shape of today's best bet.
